layout.headline: Open technology. Serious engineering. Business outcomes.
layout.subheadline: We design, build, and modernize digital platforms on open-source foundations, without the risk enterprises usually associate with 'open source.' Architecture, security, and long-term support included.
layout.side_text: A global technology consultancy working across CMS, commerce, business applications, and custom software for enterprise, government, and education clients.

layout.heading: We begin by listening -- understanding your goals.

steps.title: Discover
steps.description: Understand the goals, constraints, and systems already in place before proposing anything.

steps.title: Define
steps.description: Turn discovery into a scoped plan: what's in, what's out, and what success looks like.

steps.title: Architect
steps.description: Design the system before writing code that locks in the wrong decisions.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Iterative delivery with regular checkpoints, not a black box until launch day.

steps.title: Launch
steps.description: A deliberate rollout with the monitoring and rollback plan already in place.

steps.title: Evolve
steps.description: Ongoing support and iteration once the platform is live and being used.

items.question: Why open source instead of proprietary platforms?
items.answer: Open source gives you the flexibility to evolve the platform without vendor lock-in. We handle the part that makes enterprises hesitate: architecture, security, integration, and long-term support, so you get that flexibility with the engineering discipline you'd expect from a proprietary vendor.

items.question: What do you actually build?
items.answer: Digital experience platforms (Drupal, Payload CMS), commerce (Vendure, Medusa, Shopify), business applications (Horilla, Snipe-IT), custom software, and the cloud/DevOps foundation underneath all of it.

items.question: Do you only take on full platform builds?
items.answer: No. We take on new builds, modernizations of existing platforms, migrations, ongoing development, and staff augmentation for teams that need more engineering capacity.

items.question: How do you scope a new project?
items.answer: A short discovery phase maps requirements and dependencies, then we propose a phased delivery plan with clear milestones.

items.question: Can you take over an existing platform?
items.answer: Yes. We regularly take over platforms built by other teams, starting with an audit before any code changes.
